<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Going concern</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank&rsquo;s Management has made
an assessment of its ability to continue as a going concern and is satisfied that it has the resources to continue in business for the
foreseeable future. Furthermore, management is not aware of any material uncertainties that may cast significant doubt on the Bank&rsquo;s
ability to continue as a going concern. Therefore, these condensed separate interim Financial Statements were prepared on the going concern
basis.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Subsidiaries</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As mentioned in Note 1, the Bank performs
certain transactions through its subsidiaries.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Subsidiaries are all the entities
controlled by the Bank. An entity controls another entity when it is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns from its continuing
involvement with such other entity and has the ability to use its power to direct the operating and financing policies of such other
entity, to affect the amounts of such returns.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As provided under IAS 27 &ldquo;Consolidated
and Separate Financial Statements&rdquo;, investments in subsidiaries were accounted for using the &ldquo;equity method&rdquo;, established
in IAS 28 &ldquo;Investments in associates and joint ventures&rdquo;. When using this method, investments are initially recognized at
cost, and such amount increases or decreases to recognize investor&rsquo;s interest in profit and loss of the entity after the date of
acquisition or creation.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Shares in profit and loss of subsidiaries
and associates are recognized under &ldquo;(Loss) / income from subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures&rdquo; in the condensed separate
interim statement of income. Ownership interest in other comprehensive income of subsidiaries is accounted for under &ldquo;(Loss) /
income of the period from interest in other comprehensive income of subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures accounted for using the
participation method&rdquo;, in the condensed separate interim statement of other comprehensive income.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Transcription into books</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As of the date of issuance of these
condensed separate interim Financial Statements, they are in the process of being transcribed into the Financial Statements book (&ldquo;Libro
Balance&rdquo;) of Banco Macro SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><B><U>Standards amendments adopted
in the fiscal year</U></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Standards amendments adopted are described
in Note 3 to the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><B><U>New pronouncements</U></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">New pronouncements are described in
Note 3 to the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>4.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>CONTINGENT TRANSACTIONS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In order to meet specific financial
needs of customers, the Bank&rsquo;s credit policy also includes, among others, the granting of guarantees, securities, bonds, letters
of credit and documentary credits. The Bank is also exposed to overdrafts and unused agreed credits on credit cards of the Bank. Since
they imply a contingent obligation for the Bank, they expose the Bank to credit risks other than those recognized in the Statement of
financial position and, therefore, they are an integral part of the total risk of the Bank.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Risks related to the abovementioned
contingent transactions have been assessed and are controlled within the framework of the Bank&rsquo;s credit risk policy, as described
in Note 45 to the consolidated Financial Statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2023, already issued.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED SEPARATE INTERIM FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF JUNE 30, 2024</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>7.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>LOSS ALLOWANCE FOR EXPECTED CREDIT
                                            LOSSES ON CREDIT EXPOSURES NOT MEASURED AT FAIR VALUE THROUGH PROFIT OR LOSS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank recognizes a loss allowance
for expected credit losses on all credit exposures not measured at fair value through profit or loss, like debt instruments measured
at amortized cost, debt instruments measured at fair value through other comprehensive income, loan commitments and financial guarantee
contracts (not measured at fair value through profit or loss), contract assets and lease receivables.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Note 8 discloses financial assets
measured at fair value on a recurring basis and financial assets not recognized at fair value. This classification is made pursuant to
the expressed in Note 3 &ldquo;Basis for the preparation of these Financial Statements and applicable accounting standards&rdquo;. Additionally,
Note 8 explains the information related to the valuation process.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Moreover, considering the temporary
exclusion established by BCRA mentioned in Note 3 &ldquo;Applicable accounting standards&rdquo; the Bank applies the impairment requirements
for the recognition and measurement of a loss allowance for financial assets measured at amortized cost or at fair value through other
comprehensive income, except for public sector exposures. In addition, the Bank applies the impairment requirements for guarantees granted,
undrawn commitments of credit cards, checking account advance agreements, letter of credits, which are not recognized in the condensed
consolidated interim statement of financial position.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">For the purpose of assessing the Bank&rsquo;s
credit risk exposure and identifying material credit risk concentration, disclosures regarding credit risk of financial assets and off
balance items are as follows.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The criterion used to calculate ECL
of Financial Trusts and Corporate Bonds is based on the rating granted by risk rating agencies to each debt security type making up the
financial trusts or each corporate bond series, respectively. This means that the factor to be used will vary depending on the debt securities
holdings (A or B). The EAD is assumed to be equal to the outstanding balance.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED SEPARATE INTERIM FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF JUNE 30, 2024</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>8.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>FAIR VALUE QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE
                                            DISCLOSURES</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Note 10 to the condensed consolidated
interim Financial Statements describes the methods and assumptions used to determine the fair value, both of the financial instruments
recognized at fair value as of those not accounted for at such fair value in these condensed separate interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In addition, the Bank discloses the
relevant information as to instruments included in Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Even though the Bank&rsquo;s Management
has used its best judgment to estimate the fair values of its financial instruments, any technique to perform such estimate implies certain
inherent fragility level.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in"><U>Fair value hierarchy</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank uses the following hierarchy
to determine and disclose the fair value of financial instruments, according to the valuation technique applied:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 1: quoted prices (unadjusted) observable
                                            in active markets that the Bank accesses to at the measurement day for identical assets or
                                            liabilities. The Bank considers markets as active only if there are sufficient trading activities
                                            with respect to the volume and liquidity of the identical assets or liabilities and when
                                            there are binding and exercisable price quotes available at each period or fiscal year, as
                                            applicable.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 2: Valuation techniques for which
                                            the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination of the fair value
                                            recognized or disclosed are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly.
                                            Such inputs include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted
                                            prices for identical instruments in inactive markets and observable inputs other than quoted
                                            prices, such as interest rates and yield curves, implied volatilities, and credit spreads.
                                            In addition, adjustments to level 2 inputs may be required for the condition or location
                                            of the asset or the extent to which it relates to items that are comparable to the valued
                                            instrument. However, if such adjustments are based on unobservable inputs that are significant
                                            to the entire measurement, the Bank will classify the instruments as Level 3.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 3: Valuation techniques for which
                                            the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination of the fair value
                                            recognized or disclosed are not based on observable market information.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The following tables show the hierarchy
in the Bank&rsquo;s financial asset and liability at fair value measurement, as of June&nbsp;30, 2024 and December&nbsp;31, 2023:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED SEPARATE INTERIM FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF JUNE 30, 2024</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Note 10 to
the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements, details the valuation techniques and significant unobservable inputs used in
the valuation of assets at Level 3.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><U>Changes
in fair value levels</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank monitors the availability
of information in the market to evaluate the classification of financial instruments into the fair value hierarchy as well as the resulting
determination of transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3 at each period end.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Except for the foregoing, as of June&nbsp;30,
2024 and December&nbsp;31, 2023, the Bank has not recognized any transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>12.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>RELATED PARTIES</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">A related party is a person or entity
that is related to the Bank:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">- has
control or joint control of the Bank;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">- has
significant influence over the Bank;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">- is
a member of the key management personnel of the Bank or of a parent of the Bank;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">- members
of the same group;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">- one
entity is an associate (or an associate of a member of a group of which the other entity is a member).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Key management personnel are those
persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Bank, directly or indirectly.
The Bank considers as key management personnel, for the purposes of IAS 24, the members of the Board of Directors and the senior management
members of the Risk Management Committee, the Assets and Liabilities Committee and the Senior Credit Committee.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Fiscal years 2019 and 2020</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As decided by the Board of Directors
in the meeting held on May&nbsp;11, 2020, considering certain case law on the matter assessed by its legal counsel and tax advisors,
on May&nbsp;26 the Bank filed with the Administraci&oacute;n Federal de Ingresos P&uacute;blicos (AFIP, for its acronym in Spanish) its
annual income tax return considering the total effect of the inflation adjustment on income tax (see section a) iv) of Note 21 to the
condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements). As a result, the current income tax determined by the Bank for fiscal year 2019
amounted to 7,002,124 (not restated). The same criterion was applied to determine the annual income tax report for 2020, which generated
accrued income tax for the Bank for such fiscal year that amounted to 9,933,210 (not restated).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In addition, on July&nbsp;23, 2021,
the Bank filed a reimbursement action with the AFIP requesting that 254,305 (not restated) paid as income tax for the 2020 tax period
be reimbursed.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As to the tax periods mentioned in
previous paragraphs, on November&nbsp;1, 2021, the AFIP notified the beginning of an income tax audit, which is in progress.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Along with the filings mentioned in
the first paragraph of this section, on December&nbsp;28, 2021, the Bank filed petitions for declaratory judgment with the Federal Administrative
Contentious Court for the periods under analysis. The file 22274/2021, for the fiscal year 2019, is in process in Court No.&nbsp;12 and
the file 22278/2021, for the fiscal year 2020, is in process in Court No.&nbsp;1.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in"><U>Fiscal year 2021</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On October&nbsp;17, 2022, Banco Macro
SA filed a reimbursement action with the AFIP requesting that 382,189 (not restated) paid as income tax for the 2021 tax period be reimbursed.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF JUNE 30, 2024</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On January&nbsp;3, 2023, the AFIP
notified the beginning of an income tax audit related to the abovementioned fiscal year, which is in progress.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Fiscal year 2022</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On June&nbsp;30, 2023, Banco Macro
SA filed a reimbursement action with the AFIP requesting that 654,673 paid as income tax for the 2022 tax period be reimbursed.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Reimbursement actions &ndash; Fiscal
years 2013 to 2017 and 2018</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On October&nbsp;24, 2019, Banco Macro
SA filed with the AFIP-DGI (Argentine tax authorities) two reimbursement actions under the terms established by the first paragraph of
section 81, Law No.&nbsp;11683 requesting the reimbursement of 4,782,766 and 5,015,451 (not restated amounts) paid to tax authorities
as income tax during tax periods 2013 through 2017 and 2018, respectively, arising from the impossibility to apply the adjustment for
inflation and other adjustment mechanisms set forth by income tax Law (prior to the amendments introduced by Laws No.&nbsp;27430 and
27468 for periods 2013 through 2017, and as revised in 2019 and amended for the 2018 tax period), plus the related compensatory interest
(SIGEA [case and file management system] files No.&nbsp;19144-14224/2019 and 19144-14222/2019). Since tax authorities have not yet issued
a resolution with respect to the abovementioned claims, on August&nbsp;7, 2020, the Bank filed both reimbursement requests under the
terms of section 81, Law No.&nbsp;11683 with the Federal Contentious and Administrative Trial Courts, which are pending in Courts No.&nbsp;8
and 2 of such jurisdiction, respectively (cases No.&nbsp;11285/2020 and 11296/2020). Currently, in connection with the file for the fiscal
year 2018, the evidence stage is closed and the process for allegation was delivered.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In connection with the tax periods
mentioned in the previous paragraph, on December&nbsp;19, 2019, the AFIP notified the beginning of the income tax audit for the 2018
tax period, and on May&nbsp;3, 2021, it notified the beginning of the income tax audit for periods 2013 through 2017. On October&nbsp;4,
2021, the AFIP ended the audit for periods 2013 through 2017 as the Bank had exercised in due time its right to resort to justice, and
that the admission of reimbursement is subject to a court decision.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Statement of cash flows presents
the changes in cash and cash equivalents derived from operating activities, investing activities and financing activities during the
period. For the preparation of the statement of cash flows the Bank adopted the indirect method for Operating Activities and the direct
method for Investment Activities and Financing Activities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank considers as &ldquo;Cash
and cash equivalents&rdquo; the item Cash and deposits in banks and those financial assets that are readily convertible to known amounts
of cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Operating activities: the normal revenue-producing
                                            activities of the Bank as well as other activities that cannot qualify as investing or financing
                                            activities.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Investing activities: the acquisition,
                                            sale and disposal by other means of long-term assets and other investments not included in
                                            cash and cash equivalents.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Financing activities: activities that
                                            result in changes in the size and composition of the shareholders&acute; equity and liabilities
                                            of the Bank and that are not part of the operating or investing activities.</TD></TR></TABLE>
